key_insight: Split complex-valued PINNs model real and imaginary parts separately to better capture oscillatory, phase-dependent PDE dynamics with improved accuracy over standard real-valued PINNs.
engineering_relevance: This offers a more accurate and general surrogate framework for forward and inverse fluid and nonlinear PDEs, especially for high-frequency, multiscale, and complex-valued engineering flows.
method: Use complex-valued network parameters and latent states.
Apply split activations independently to real and imaginary components for stability and efficiency.
Train on physics residuals for both forward and inverse PDE identification.
evidence_signal: The paper reports evaluation on many benchmarks, including nonlinear Schrödinger, KdV, Navier-Stokes, and Beltrami flow, with the Beltrami case reaching a relative L2 error of 4.07×10^-5 and generally outperforming RV-PINNs.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the chosen split activation and collocation sampling strategy, so gains are not guaranteed without careful tuning.
paper_title: Split Complex-Valued Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Forward and Inverse Nonlinear PDEs
